npcs.name: Adria the Witch
npcs.role: Witch of Tristram who lives in a hut across the stream southeast of town. She is the only source of Mana potions and offers a constant, diverse supply of magical items, Identify scrolls and Town Portal spells.
npcs.motivation: Wants to keep trading magic goods to those who go down into the dungeon. She recharges staffs at a very reasonable price and warns adventurers about the Butcher. Once the party reaches the Hell levels she stocks Elixirs at 5,000 Gold each.

leverage.vulnerability: Her trade depends on adventurers returning alive from the dungeon, and the Town Portal is the primary means of travel between dungeon and town.
leverage.bribe: Gold; she sells rare Spellbooks and Scrolls that do not sell cheap.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Adria is the one to see when the subject is Magic." | Subtext: She knows her stock is the only real source of Mana and Town Portals, and she expects to be paid for it.
npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: Diablo
npcs.role: The demon at the bottom of the dungeon, the source of its monsters and the central foe of the game. He commands the Servants of Darkness and the Unique monsters, and the final showdown is with him on Level 16.
npcs.motivation: Directs his minions and Unique creatures from the deepest, darkest dungeon level. The town's survival depends on the party facing him.

leverage.vulnerability: Lore says that with the guide's help 'the demon Diablo doesn't stand a chance in hell'; he can be finished off after many attempts at his door.
leverage.bribe: None; he laughs at players who waste their gold too early.

npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: Pepin
npcs.role: The Healer of Tristram. He sells potions and scrolls for healing, restores the party to full health for no charge, and gives the Poisoned Water Supply quest. His house lies near the fissure that leads back to hell from dungeon level 13.
npcs.motivation: Wants the party to stop the sickness spreading through town from a fouled water supply, tainted by a demon infestation on Level 2. He rewards them with the Ring of Truth once the set piece is cleared.

leverage.vulnerability: The town's sickness from the poisoned water, which he cannot cure himself.
leverage.bribe: Completing his quest; he rewards the party with the Ring of Truth.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Pepin can heal what ails you." | Subtext: He offers care freely, but the real sickness is the poisoned water, and he needs someone to go and fix it.
npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: Griswold
npcs.role: The Blacksmith of Tristram. He keeps a store of intriguing (and often expensive) weapons and armor, and repairs items whose Durability has worn down.
npcs.motivation: Makes his living selling weapons and armor and repairing items. His list of stock changes as the party buys things or advances an experience level, and he charges a premium for percentage adjustments.

leverage.vulnerability: His income depends on adventurers returning with worn gear, and his repair prices run highest for magical or Unique items.
leverage.bribe: Gold; common items are repaired for next-to-nothing.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Griswold's services are indispensable." | Subtext: He knows the party cannot do without his forge and prices accordingly.
npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: Ogden the Tavern Owner
npcs.role: The Tavern Owner, one of Tristram's bit players. He occasionally begins a quest or divulges semi-useful information, and tells the story of King Leoric.
npcs.motivation: Wants the tavern sign back from the demons, and begs the party to put King Leoric's soul at ease by destroying his now-cursed form. If the sign is returned he rummages around and produces the Harlequin Crest.

leverage.vulnerability: He has lost his tavern sign to the demons and fears the cursed king.
leverage.bribe: Returning the sign; he will produce the Harlequin Crest in return.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Put his soul at ease by destroying his now-cursed form." | Subtext: He wants Leoric's curse lifted but is not willing to face the king himself.
npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: The Butcher
npcs.role: A sadistic demon on Level 2, a Unique monster in the Butcher quest and an Overlord with an attitude and a mean cleaver. He waits in a large room and rushes out to greet the player when it is opened.
npcs.motivation: Delights in torture and pain, and dismembers opponents with his huge Cleaver. Sorcerers and Rogues tend to lose limbs quickly early on.

leverage.vulnerability: He cannot open doors; the party can lure him to a doorway flanked by steel grating, close the door in his face and shoot him with a bow.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "is a sadistic creature that delights in the torture and pain of others." | Subtext: Adria's warning; he is a serious threat to beginners and the level should be cleared before opening his room.
npcs.notes: Adria the Witch describes him to the party. His position in the dungeon varies from game to game.

npcs.name: King Leoric
npcs.role: A former king, driven mad by grief over his kidnapped son and destroyed by his knights and priest. He cursed the town and his former followers on death, and now rules a legion of undead in the labyrinth.
npcs.motivation: Wound: lost his son to kidnappers, which drove him mad. Want: rest for his soul, freed from his cursed form. He conjures Skeletons during the fight, and his death drops the Skeleton Crown.

leverage.vulnerability: Killing him quickly prevents an unstoppable horde of bonemen; Holy Bolt is recommended against him.
leverage.bribe: None; destroying his cursed form puts his soul at ease.

npcs.notes: Cramped quarters make it impossible for low-level characters to avoid damage.

npcs.name: Cain the Storyteller
npcs.role: The town Elder of Tristram, who stands near the central fountain. He advises the party on the hidden capabilities of unidentified magical items.
npcs.motivation: Wants to pass on what he knows to anyone patient enough to stop and listen. He thinks the demons may deem Ogden's sign sacred and powerful, like the sun, which they fear.

leverage.vulnerability: Depends on visitors being patient enough to listen to him.
leverage.bribe: Gold for his identify service, which costs the same as the Witch's Identify scroll.

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Cain has a lot to tell anyone patient enough to stop and listen." | Subtext: He holds knowledge the party needs, but he will share it only with those who give him time.
npcs.notes: Faction chosen as the closest of the available options, since none is explicit in the lore.

npcs.name: Wirt
npcs.role: The peg-legged boy who sells a single rotating item for 50 gold pieces, whispering for attention across the stream behind Gillian's house
npcs.motivation: Wound: gnawed on by monsters, he escaped the dungeon with his life. Allegiance: himself, nobody's friend. He trades one new treasure at random intervals, and buying a cheap item from him coaxes him into restocking.

leverage.vulnerability: Gnawed on by monsters; he is a crippled boy living alone in a small clearing beneath a tree
leverage.bribe: 50 gold pieces to see his current item; buying even a cheap scroll prompts him to restock

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Wirt is nobody's friend, but he might have just the weapon you need." | Subtext: He deals only for himself, and the price of his goods is gold.

npcs.name: Archbishop Lazarus
npcs.role: An archbishop who led the townspeople down to find the lost prince and walked them into a trap
npcs.motivation: Led the people below to find the lost prince, but the descent ended in a trap where a demon he called the Butcher killed them. What he really wants and what he hides are not stated; the survivors name him a bastard.

secretsKnown.secret: He led the townspeople into a trap where they were killed by the demon he called the Butcher

leverage.vulnerability: The Wounded Townsman accuses him of betraying the people he led down

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "The Archbishop Lazarus, he led us down here to find the lost prince. The bastard led us into a trap!" | Subtext: The survivors blame him for the deaths, and what he knows about the trap is something he would rather hide.

npcs.name: Snotspill
npcs.role: A disgusting little creature who guards the way to the Level 5 down staircase on Dungeon Level 4
npcs.motivation: Want: keep the tavern sign and the power he believes it grants. He and his friends believe the sign gives them great power. If the player gives him the sign he will thank them, and then must be killed for a random item.

leverage.vulnerability: His belief that the stolen tavern sign gives him great power
leverage.bribe: Ogden's sign; he thanks the giver and then can be killed for a random item

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Snotspill and his friends believe the Tavern sign gives them great power." | Subtext: He will not let the sign go unless the party deals with him, and the sign is his weak point.

npcs.name: Gillian
npcs.role: A beloved townswoman of Tristram and a bit player whose house lies behind the stream where Wirt whispers
npcs.motivation: Allegiance: Tristram. She occasionally begins a quest or divulges semi-useful information, but generally fills in details of stories other citizens initiate.

leverage.vulnerability: Her love for Tristram and its people

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Gillian is beloved in Tristram, but her role in Diablo is that of a bit player" | Subtext: She seldom drives events herself but knows details that fill in the stories of others.

npcs.name: Farnham
npcs.role: A Tristram bit player, the Town Drunk, who occasionally begins a quest or divulges semi-useful information
npcs.motivation: His story is a sad one, when it is coherent at all. The lore does not say what he wants or hides.

leverage.vulnerability: Drink, and a sad story he can barely tell coherently

dialogueHooks: Spoken: "Farnham's story is a sad one, when it's coherent at all." | Subtext: There is real grief behind the drunken rambling, and the party must piece it together.

quests.title: Whispers of Dark Riders
quests.name: Whispers of Dark Riders
quests.notes: The party arrives in twilit Tristram and learns what the townsfolk fear before going down into the cathedral labyrinth.

steps.title: Listen to the townsfolk
steps.text: Speak with the anxious villagers about the dark riders and the strange rituals at the ruined cathedral.

steps.title: Reach the cathedral
steps.text: Approach the ruined cathedral at the edge of the village and find the dying townsman at its entrance.

quests.title: Avenge the Fallen: The Butcher
quests.name: Avenge the Fallen: The Butcher
quests.notes: A dying townsman says Archbishop Lazarus led them into a trap and begs for vengeance against the Butcher. Crucible 'The Cleaver Corrupts': a hero who keeps the Cleaver feeds the Cleaver Corruption clock.

steps.title: Hear the townsman's plea
steps.text: The dying man says Lazarus led them into a trap and asks you to avenge them.

steps.title: Trap the Butcher at the grating
steps.text: Clear the level, lure the Butcher to the grated doorway, close the door on him and shoot him with a bow.

steps.title: Decide the Cleaver's fate
steps.text: Take the Butcher's Cleaver. If a hero keeps wielding it instead of a weapon suited to their class, the demons notice and the townsfolk grow afraid.

quests.title: The Fouled Spring
quests.name: The Fouled Spring
quests.notes: Goat Demons and the Fallen Ones gang up in the set-piece caverns beyond the crack in the wall. Clearing them purifies the spring and Pepin rewards the party with the Ring of Truth.

steps.title: Find the crack in the wall
steps.text: Locate the passage labeled 'To A Dark Passage' on Level 2 and enter the caverns.

steps.title: Break the Goat Demons and the Fallen
steps.text: Fight through the Fallen Ones and the Goat Demon, who gang up on you.

steps.title: Clear the last monster
steps.text: Drop the last of the level's monsters and the waterway runs blue again. Return to Pepin for the Ring of Truth.

quests.title: Reading the Pattern
quests.name: Reading the Pattern
quests.notes: Crucible 'Reading the Pattern': the party heeds Adria and links the stolen sign, the fouled spring and the dark riders, then looks for whoever directs the demons before descending further.

steps.title: Heed Adria's warning
steps.text: Adria warns that the demons' erratic behavior may be deliberate. Compare notes with Cain on the riders, the poisoned spring and the stolen sign.

steps.title: Trace the directing hand
steps.text: Follow the connections back to Lazarus and what lies below him, in the cathedral depths.

quests.title: The Curse of King Leoric
quests.name: The Curse of King Leoric
quests.notes: Ogden asks the party to put King Leoric's soul at ease by destroying his cursed form in his tomb, reached from Level 3.

steps.title: Hear Ogden's tale
steps.text: Ogden recounts Leoric's story and implores you to destroy his cursed form.

steps.title: Break the crucified Skeletons
steps.text: Destroy each crucified Skeleton in the corners of the large room. The last one opens a secret antechamber in the northern wall.

steps.title: Destroy King Leoric
steps.text: Put him down quickly before the summoned Skeletons overwhelm you, and take the Skeleton Crown.

quests.title: Ogden's Stolen Sign
quests.name: Ogden's Stolen Sign
quests.notes: Demons stole the sign of the Rising Sun Inn and Tavern, and Snotspill blocks the stairs to Level 5 until it is claimed. Crucible 'The Sign Surrendered': giving the sign and the Harlequin Crest to Snotspill convinces his demons the sign has made them powerful.

steps.title: Learn of the theft
steps.text: Ogden tells you demons have stolen his tavern's sign.

steps.title: Confront Snotspill
steps.text: Find Snotspill in his set piece on Dungeon Level 4. He will not let you reach the stairs to Level 5 until the sign is claimed.

steps.title: Return it or surrender it
steps.text: Return the sign to Ogden, or hand it with the Harlequin Crest to Snotspill and leave his demons believing it has made them powerful.

items.name: Ring of Truth
items.specs: Unique ring. -3 armor and -1 to damage received. Absorbs one Hit Point per strike received. Adds +10 to overall resistance and Hit Points.
items.notes: Given by Pepin the Healer as the reward for completing the Poisoned Water Supply quest in the caverns below Level 2.

items.name: Harlequin Crest
items.specs: Faster attack; knocks back monsters; mana +20; HP -20.
items.notes: Ogden the Tavern Owner hands it over when the player returns the stolen tavern sign to him instead of giving it to Snotspill. Reward of Ogden's Sign quest.

items.name: The Butcher's Cleaver
items.specs: Unique heavy, axe-like weapon. Kills most monsters with a single swipe for the next couple of levels, after which a weapon suited to the character's class should replace it.
items.notes: Wielded by the Butcher and dropped when he is slain on Level 2.

items.name: Ogden's sign
items.specs: The stolen sign of the Rising Sun Inn and Tavern. Snotspill and his demon friends believe it gives them great power.
items.notes: Sits in a large chest in Snotspill's set piece on Dungeon Level 4 and must be acquired to open the way down. It belongs to Ogden the Tavern Owner; return it to him or give it to Snotspill.

items.name: Scroll of Healing
items.specs: Heals without spending Mana, and unlike potions it can be hotkeyed, which is a huge advantage in combat.
items.notes: Sold by the healer (Pepin) and the witch (Adria) in Tristram for 50 gold pieces each. Supply is not limitless, so stock up and keep only enough, since scrolls are needed in ever-increasing numbers.

items.name: Potion of Full Rejuvenation
items.specs: Fully replenishes both Health and Mana in one potion: the most economical potion in terms of space.
items.notes: Sold by the Healer (Pepin) or the Witch (Adria) for 600 Gold each, more than the guide thinks worth paying.

items.name: Elixir
items.specs: Increases Strength, Magic or Dexterity by one point each.
items.notes: Once the Hell levels are reached, Adria and Pepin begin to stock random Elixirs at 5,000 Gold each.

items.name: Identify scroll
items.specs: Identifies magical items in the dungeon, so magical gear can be used without taking it back to Tristram to see Cain.
items.notes: Sold by Adria the Witch at her hut. The price is the same as getting the service from Cain.

items.name: Mana potions
items.notes: Adria the Witch's hut in Tristram is the only place the player can purchase Mana potions.

items.name: Healing potions and scrolls
items.specs: Potions and scrolls for healing; miscellaneous elixirs are thrown in late in the game for variety.
items.notes: Peddled by Pepin the Healer in Tristram.

items.name: Ressurect scrolls
items.specs: Scrolls that revive a fallen hero.
items.notes: In multiplayer games, Pepin the Healer in Tristram carries a steady supply.

items.name: Scroll of Mana Shield
items.specs: Lets the Sorcerer cast Mana Shield from a scroll. The spell wears off when using Town Portal or traveling between levels.
items.notes: Obtained from the witch in Tristram. Cast it only when staying a while at a level.

items.name: Skeleton Crown
items.notes: Drops when King Leoric dies in Leoric's Tomb, reached from Level 3. Reward for ending the Curse of King Leoric quest.

items.name: Bow
items.specs: Ranged physical weapon, the chosen and preferred weapon of the Rogue, who fires it very quickly and accurately. Needs high Dexterity for effective standard combat, and Strength to use larger bows. Prevents a Warrior from using a shield. Any character can fire through a grating or fence to damage a horde.
items.notes: The Rogue should find one in the dungeon or buy one as soon as possible, selling everything early on to afford a decent bow.

items.name: The Constricting Ring
items.specs: Unique ring. Resist all +75%, increasing overall resistance by 75%. The wearer constantly loses life and takes 1 to 2 hp each time they are hit.

trackers.name: The Cleaver's Hunger
trackers.notes: Crucible 'The Cleaver Corrupts'. Rises while a hero keeps wielding the Butcher's Cleaver. Demons notice it and townsfolk grow afraid.

consequences.description: Townsfolk fear the hero. Cain withdraws to the tavern.
The Cleaver's brutality draws Lazarus's notice, and he waits in the dungeon.

trackers.name: Poison in the Spring
trackers.notes: The fouled water spreads sickness through Tristram until the caverns are cleared.

consequences.description: Pepin is overwhelmed with the sick and stays in Tristram.
The poisoning breaks the town's resolve, and the demons' foothold in the caverns holds.

trackers.name: The Skeleton Horde
trackers.notes: Leoric summons Skeletons the longer he lives.

consequences.description: The horde swells beyond control and Leoric retreats into the catacombs.

trackers.name: The Sign of Power
trackers.notes: Crucible 'The Sign Surrendered'. Rises if the sign is surrendered to Snotspill and his demons believe it empowers them.

consequences.description: Snotspill's emboldened demons spread beyond his lair.
Emboldened by the sign, the demons claim Ogden's tavern.

trackers.name: Darkness Beneath the Cathedral
trackers.notes: Whatever directs the demons draws closer to Tristram with each descent. Uncovering the pattern pushes it back, and surrendering power to the demons advances it.

consequences.description: Lazarus withdraws deeper to prepare the ritual.
Diablo's influence reaches the town and Tristram's survival is in doubt.

factions.name: Sisters of the Sightless Eye
factions.description: One of the mysterious Sisters of the Sightless Eye, the Rogue's "sixth sense" allows her to perceive and disarm traps before they spring. The order is known for this uncanny sixth sense for traps; the Rogue is its known member.
factions.notes: Also known as the Sightless Eye. The source gives no leader, headquarters or relations with other factions.

factions.name: Brotherhood of the Vizjerei
factions.description: An order of magic-users. The Sorcerer is a member of the Brotherhood of the Vizjerei, and is especially adept at utilizing scrolls and spells.
factions.notes: The source gives no further details about the Brotherhood: no leader, headquarters, allies or relations with other factions.

creatures.name: Acid Beasts
creatures.summary: Often the first creature met with something like ranged magic. They vomit globs of acid that damage on contact and then form a puddle at the victim's feet that keeps damaging until it dissipates. Upper-end beasts (Poison Spitter, Pit Beast, Lava Maw) are strong enough to convulse the victim in agony. Fight from a distance but never stand still.

senses.blindspots: Inferred: they spit in the player's direction and cannot answer fast, mobile targets.

anatomicalWeakSpots: They get corralled behind fences and can be chipped away at from range.

disposition.ethologySummary: Swarming pack (S:3), Local Grazer or Scavenger (E:2), Feral Instinct (C:1)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Acid-spitting swarms make corridors hazardous; travelers hire ranged guards, and stationary parties die in the poison.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Spit at the first target in range; keep spitting while it stays still.

cues.label: Is a target within spit range?
Is the target standing in the puddle?

signatureActions.name: Acid Glob
signatureActions.effect: Vomit a glob of acid that damages on contact, then forms a puddle at the target's feet that keeps damaging until it dissipates. Poison balls fall to the ground after a certain distance.

signatureActions.name: Agonizing Spit
signatureActions.trigger: Upper-end beasts spit goo in the player's direction
signatureActions.effect: Acid strong enough to convulse the victim in agony.

instinctiveQuirks: Swarm and spit rather than close to melee.
Get corralled behind fences and can be chipped away at.
spoorAndSigns: Lingering acid puddles and splashes of goo on the floor.
vocalizations: Inferred: wet retching as they vomit acid.
vernacularFolklore: Stay mobile, or die.

creatures.name: Advocate
creatures.summary: A demonic spellcaster, a variant of the Counselors, resistant to fire and lightning and immune to magic. It fights with a Flash Spell, which a Golem is immune to. The card's table entry is partly garbled, so details are thin.

senses.blindspots: Inferred: nothing in canon; relies on spell range rather than close awareness.

defenses.armorType: Unarmoured demonic hide, warded against spells
anatomicalWeakSpots: Inferred: it is a caster, so it is weakest when closed on in melee and denied room to cast.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Rigid Scripted Instinct (C:3)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Travellers hire spell-wise guards or a construct escort before using corridors where advocates are reported; unescorted wanderers avoid the path.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Casts at the first visible target that is not immune to its spell.

cues.label: Is the target a golem or spell-immune?

signatureActions.trigger: A valid target comes into view
signatureActions.effect: Looses a flash of magic at the target; a Golem is immune to it.

instinctiveQuirks: Inferred: shuns foes it cannot harm with spells.
spoorAndSigns: Inferred: scorched stone and lingering magical residue.
vocalizations: Inferred: low chanting before a cast.
vernacularFolklore: Fighters say 'the Golem is particularly effective against advocates'.

harvestYields.component: Inferred: arcane residue from the demon's body

creatures.name: Animal-based monsters
creatures.summary: A monster category of the dungeon including winged beasties that swarm and flutter through it.

senses.blindspots: Inferred; none recorded.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Inferred: winged beasties are fragile once caught.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Group (S:3), Local Grazer or Scavenger (E:2), Feral and Chaotic (C:1)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Swarms are a pest to travelers; casualties happen but routes stay open.

instinctiveQuirks: Winged beasties swarm and flutter through the dungeon.
spoorAndSigns: Fluttering wings in the dark.
vernacularFolklore: Counted among the three broad monster categories of the Servants of Darkness: the Undead, Animal-based monsters, and Demons.

creatures.name: Archers
creatures.summary: Monsters that attack from a distance. They swarm closer to town, and the deeper the dungeon goes, the more likely their ranged attacks carry a magical component.

senses.blindspots: Inferred: weak once an enemy closes to melee range.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Inferred: they are exposed once an enemy closes the distance and they lose their range advantage.

disposition.ethologySummary: Structured Pack (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Swarms near town make the approach to the dungeon a gauntlet; travelers hire shield-bearers and avoid open sightlines.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Loose at the first visible target within range.

cues.label: Is a target in line of sight at range?
Is an enemy in melee reach?

signatureActions.name: Volley
signatureActions.effect: Ranged attack from a distance; deeper in the dungeon the shot gains a magical component.

signatureActions.name: Swarm Fire
signatureActions.effect: Many archers concentrate ranged attacks together.

instinctiveQuirks: Keeps its distance and attacks from range
Attacks gain a magical component the lower one goes
spoorAndSigns: Spent missiles scattered along sightlines (inferred)
vernacularFolklore: Swarms of archers appear closer to town; the lower the player goes, the more likely a distance attack is magical.

creatures.name: Balrogs
creatures.summary: Some of the toughest villains in the game. Magic-resistant and immune to fire, their onslaught cannot be withstood for long. Variants are Slayer, Guardian, Vortex Lord and Balrog.

senses.blindspots: Card silent; inferred none notable.

defenses.armorType: Heavy demonic hide (inferred from armor comparable to the player's own)
anatomicalWeakSpots: No anatomical weak spot is named; a devastating non-flaming ranged attack is the answer.

disposition.ethologySummary: Solitary (S:1), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Adaptive Instinct (C:2)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Their onslaught cannot be withstood for long; parties without a ranged, non-flaming answer abandon the corridor and detour.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Press the onslaught the moment initiative is held.

cues.label: Has the Balrog seized the initiative?
Is the foe within reach?

signatureActions.name: Relentless onslaught
signatureActions.effect: Its assault cannot be withstood for long; the player must retreat hastily.

instinctiveQuirks: Seize the initiative and overwhelm
vernacularFolklore: Some of the toughest villains in the game, the Balrogs mean business.

creatures.name: Bats
creatures.summary: A common, small, swooping creature that tends to swarm. The tougher variants (Fiend, Blink Bat, Gloom, Familiar) inflict considerable damage in swarms, and each type has its own attack. Best handled by breaking off and drawing them through a narrow opening to pick them off singly.

senses.blindspots: Inferred: erratic swoops leave them funnelled by narrow openings and easy to pick off one at a time.

anatomicalWeakSpots: Fragile small bodies; once drawn through a narrow opening they can be killed singly.

disposition.ethologySummary: Swarming pack (S:3), Active Ranging Hunter (E:3), Feral Instinct (C:1)

gigerenzerBehavior.dreadEffect: Swarms are a nuisance on dungeon routes; travelers lose time and blood but corridors stay open, though the lightning-using Familiars make guards wary.

heuristicProfile.stoppingRule: Attack whatever the swarm is already swooping at; break off only when the target retreats through a narrow opening.
